links.reason: The shared close is real and near-verbatim: 348 செந்நுதல் யானை பிணிப்ப, வருந்தல மன் எம் பெருந்துறை மரனே and 347 வினைநவில் யானை பிணிப்ப, வேர்துளங் கினநம் ஊருள் மரனே, both under மகட்பாற் காஞ்சி. But teaches adds that the image avoids blaming the girl, which 348 does not bear out: ஈனா ளாயினள் ஆயின் places the cause in her very birth, and 347's line 8 is lost so its view of her cannot be read; two poems also do not make a 'stock' way.
links.text_issue: purananuru:347 line 8 and part of line 9 are lost.

links.reason: There is no shared distinctive image; what the two share is the colophon thurai உண்டாட்டு, the victory feast. 262 orders the feast (நறவும் தொடுமின்; விடையும் வீழ்மின்) for the lord returning நிரையோடு, and 269's turn to இக் கருங்கை வாளே after a request for பிழிமகிழ் is uncertain in syntax (என்ப). 'Drink bound to the deed, a rite of reward' restates what the thurai already means.

Both are about love's separation, so this is not a different domain. 23 is a paalai separation for wealth (ஆண்டுச்செய் பொருளே, the token மௌவல் on the nochi) and 24 a mullai separation in a king's camp (வேந்தன் பாசறையேமே), so the poems have different couples and different causes, and neither 'supplies the half' of the other except by being placed next to it. Home and camp seen side by side is the stock pattern of the mullai camp poem, and 24 already holds both halves (தம்ஊரோளே ... யாமே).

335 states as the land's one rite that no god is worshipped with paddy except the stone (கல்லே பரவின் அல்லது, நெல்உகுத்துப் பரவும் கடவுளும் இலவே), and 263 turns that into a command to a passing drummer (தொழாதனை கழிதல் ஓம்புமதி) at a stone on a road (இவ் வறநிலை யாறே). The general fact and the obligation on a traveller make a real development. The note's 'such a stone' glosses over a difference: 263's man fell recovering a herd (பல்லாத் திரள்நிரை பெயர்தர), not killing an elephant.
links.text_issue: purananuru:335 lines 1-2 are broken; one flower name is lost.

links.reason: 797 is about fools as persons (பேதையார் கேண்மை ஒரீஇ விடல்), and 805 is about a painful act by a friend, to be read as either பேதைமை or பெருங்கிழமை (ஒன்றோ ... என்றுணர்க). The note drops the second option. One verse is about choosing friends and the other about bearing with old ones, which is different advice for different situations; 805 limits 797 and does not contradict it. 'The same பேதைமை' equates a person's nature with a single act.

The name-mirror is real: in 67 the swan's only credential is இரும்பிசிர் ஆந்தை அடியுறை, and in 216 the unseen friend calls himself பேதைச் சோழன் and the king says இன்னே வருகுவன். But 216 never names its friend, and its colophon gives no patron. That the friend is Pisirandhaiyar, and so that this is 'one friendship from both sides', comes from tradition, not from the poems or the packet's colophons.

Both are the stock thurai மகட் போக்கிய தாய் சொல்லியது, by different poets. 263's regret (அவள் துணிவு அறிந்தனென் ஆயின் ... இனிதினிற் புணர்க்குவென் மன்னே) and 275's sand house (என்மகள் ... வண்டலும் காண்டீரோ) are two variants of one situation; neither extends the other. The 'authority' reading fits 263, but 275 shows scolding too (யாம்தற் கழறுங் காலை), so the split into two kinds of answer is the grader's typology, not something the pair teaches.

Ezhini is named in both, with spear and horse: 158 has ஊராது ஏந்திய குதிரைக், கூர்வேல் ... எழினியும் among the seven dead givers, and Ak 105 has சில்பரிக் குதிரை, பல்வேல் எழினி, whose men 'finish his commissioned work' (விடுதொழில் முடிமார்) by driving cattle across the frontier on the eloping daughter's road. The note says what the akam poet does with the name, and the giver-versus-raider contrast is specific. One caveat: 158's 'horse not ridden' may be a hill named Kuthirai, so the horse epithet is less firmly shared than the name and spear.

Pannan of Sirukudi is named in both (சிறுகுடி கிழான் பண்ணன்; 173 பசிப்பிணி மருத்துவன் இல்லம்), and both make him the cure for hunger, so the link is real. But teaches overreaches. 'A crowned Chola king' comes only from 173's colophon. The oath in 388 (பாடேன் ஆயின் ... வழுதி, கண்மா றிலியர்என் பெருங்கிளைப் புரவே) is hard to construe, since -இலியர் is a negative optative. And nothing in either poem says Pannan 'outranked kings'.
links.text_issue: purananuru:388 lines 8-11 can be construed more than one way.

links.reason: The ideas really meet: Ak 243 ends அனைத்தால் தோழி! நம் தொல்வினைப் பயனே through பனிவார் கண்ணேம், and Naladiyar 110 argues from a fixed lot (சிறுகாலைப் பட்ட பொறி) that grief is pointless (இறுகாலத் தென்னை பரிவு). The contrast in attitude is real. But the note's 'both name former deeds' overstates the Naladiyar, which names a mark set early, not deeds. Neither verse limits the other: the Naladiyar turns the akam speaker's explanation into a consolation, which is closer to develops.

Both cut giving loose from reward in the next world: 134 says Ay is not அறவிலை வணிகன் who says இம்மைச் செய்தது மறுமைக்கு ஆம், and Kural 222 says மேலுலகம் இல்லெனினும் ஈதலே நன்று. Teaches correctly names what each puts in the reward's place: 134 சான்றோர் சென்ற நெறி (custom) and the Kural a bare judgment. That is specific and true of both.

The tuft is genuinely shared (279 பாறுமயிர்க் குடுமி எண்ணெய் நீவி; 310 மான்உளை அன்ன குடுமி), as is a young son going to war after a father's death (279 இவள்கொழுநன் ... ஆண்டுப்பட் டனனே; 310 முன்நாள் வீழ்ந்த உரவோர் மகனே). But these are poems by different poets under different thurai, and teaches builds a story out of them that it admits the anthology never states. 'Comes back to lie on the shield' is the grader's construction, not a development in the poems.

Both Paranar marutham poems use Pazhaiyan of Por: 186 போஒர் அன்ன, என் செறிவளை உடைத்தலோ இலனே (unbroken like his fort), and 326 பழையன் ஓக்கிய வேல்போற் பிழையல கண் (unmissing like his spear). The note is accurate, and teaches is specific and true: one patron's fame gives the courtesan's boast its firmness and the friend's praise its sure aim.

The phrasing is closely parallel: Ak 54 தனக்கென வாழாப் பிறர்க்கு உரியாளன் / பண்ணன் and Pur 182 தமக்கென முயலா நோன்தாள், பிறர்க்கென முயலுநர். The general ideal on which 182 rests the world is applied in 54 to one named patron. 'Already' implies a chronology that cannot be fixed, but the point that the maxim served as praise of a real patron holds.

The scene is shared: a chieftain met as a hunter (150 ஓர் வல்வில் வேட்டுவன்; 152 வல்வில் வேட்டம்) feeds the bard from his kill. Teaches errs twice. The colophons give வன் பரணர் and வண்பரணர், most likely one poet, not 'two poets'. And in 152 the gift does not come before the giver is known: the bards guess ஓரி கொல்லோ and hail him கோ before he gives (தன்பெயர் ஆகலின் நாணி), so 'proved genuine by being given before the giver is known' fits only 150.

The half-line is nearly identical: 27 மரைஇலை போல மாய்ந்திசினோர் பலரே and Naladiyar 359 மரையிலையின் மாய்ந்தார் பலர். Teaches is specific and true. In 27 the leaf stands against the full flower (நூற்றிதழ் அலரின் நிறை) and the few with உரையும் பாட்டும், so the leaf's death is death without a name. The Naladiyar moves the phrase to people whose hopes came to nothing.

The shared formula is real (Ak 6 மாவண் தித்தன் பிண்ட நெல்லின் உறந்தை; Pur 352 மாவண் தித்தன் வெண்ணெல் வேலி உறந்தை), both by Paranar. But 'refused bride-price' rests on a broken line (கொடுப்பவும் கொளாஅ னெ. . . .) plus the thurai மகட்பாற் காஞ்சி: who refuses, and what, cannot be read. The closing 'how much shared fame the two kinds drew on' is the general point, not something this pair shows.

A distinctive detail is shared by two poets: 280 சிறுவெள் ஆம்பல் அல்லி உண்ணும் கழிகல மகளிர் with மழித்தலை, and 250 கூந்தல் கொய்து, குறுந்தொடு நீக்கி, அல்லி உணவின் மனைவி. Teaches is true: alli food appears in both as a public mark of widowhood, and in 280 the wife foresees her own state through it (வழிநினைந்து இருத்தல், அதனினும் அரிதே).

Both turn on விழுப்புண் (93 line 15; Kural 776), and 93 records the rite of cutting a body that died of sickness on grass so it may go where heroes go (வாள்போழ்ந்து அடக்கலும்). The note misdescribes it, though: the poem says the fleeing kings escaped (உய்ந்தனர்) that rite by dying on Anji's field. It does not 'tell how a king was cut'. And the claim that the Kural's ledger of days 'rests on' a belief about the afterlife is not in 776, which speaks only of days without a wound.
links.text_issue: purananuru:93 lines 2-11 are compressed in syntax.

links.reason: The spring signs are shared (355 மாவும் வண்தளிர் ஈன்றன குயிலும் ... நுவலும்; 341 குயிலும் தேம்பாய் மாஅத்து ஓங்குசினை விளிக்கும்), but they are the stock marks of the season. The two responses differ because the situations differ, as the colophons show: in 355 he has only announced his going (பிரிவுணர்த்திய) and she plans a reproach (புலந்தனம் வருகம்), while 341 speaks during the separation (உய்தகை இன்றால்). So the pair does not show that the response was free of the season's cue.

Athiral dressed in the heroine's முச்சி is shared (391 அதிரல் ... புணர்ந்தோர் புனைந்தவென் பொதிமாண் முச்சி; 393 வேனில் அதிரல் வேய்ந்தநின் ... முச்சி), a meaningful shared image. But these are different poets and different couples, so it is not 'the same token' turned by the friend. The note also inverts 393's close: நீடலர் ... இன்துயில் மறந்தே means he will not linger forgetting that sleep, not that he has forgotten it.

The lighthouse is distinctive and shared: Perumpanatruppadai has வேயா மாடத்து இரவின் மாட்டிய இலங்குசுடர் ஞெகிழி calling ஓடுகலம் to the துறை, and Ak 255 has நீகான் மாட ஒள்எரி மருங்கு அறிந்து ஒய்ய. Teaches is true: the idyll describes the light as a feature of the port, and the akam poem makes it the figure of a sure arrival, set against the lack of anyone to carry word (உரையொடு செல்லும் அன்பினர்ப் பெறினே).

The hero-stone is genuinely shared: 265 கல் ஆயினையே, and Kural 771 பலரென்னை முன்நின்று கல்நின் றவர். The perspective contrast in teaches is true: in 771 the stone is the enemy's fate, while in 265 the bards' wealth (பரிசிலர் செல்வம்) went with the dead lord. But 265 places no limit or condition on 771; the pair is a shared image seen from two sides.

The phrase is shared (18 நீர்இன்று அமையா யாக்கைக்கு; Kural 20 நீர்இன்று அமையாது உலகு), and the conclusions really diverge. The Kural makes everything depend on the sky (வான்இன்று அமையாது ஒழுக்கு). Pur 18 says land that sows and looks to the sky (வித்திவான் நோக்கும் புன்புலம்) does not serve the king, and orders tanks built (நீர்நிலை பெருக). Teaches names that divergence precisely.

Thondi is named in both (48 கானல்அம் தொண்டி; அஃதுஎம் ஊரே; Ak 60 திண்தேர்ப் பொறையன் தொண்டி அன்னஎம் ஒண்தொடி). But 'town X அன்ன' is the commonest akam comparison, and teaches says only that akam poets used a famous town as a byword for wealth. It misses what Ak 60 actually does with Thondi: lines 1-6 fill the town with a fisher girl feeding her father, a shore life and not royal glory. The note's 'bangles' also takes ஒண்தொடி literally where it likely names the girl.

Both are the same love-book situation, a man longing for an evening at home: Kural 1268 மனைகலந்து மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து, and Ak 9 கன்றுபுகு மாலை நின்றோள் எய்தி. Teaches misattributes the eye-covering to the woman's side, when it is the man's heart that steals up (கைகவியாச் சென்று, கண் புதையாக் குறுகி); only the lizard-omen prayer (பல்லி படுதொறும் பரவி) is hers. The Kural's speaker is also disputed, as its own nuance says.

No image is shared, and the link rests on 224's colophon. The poem never names Karikalan; its patron line does. Ak 55's puram image is about Cheralathan and the worthies who died with him (வான்வடக் கிருந்தென ... அவனொடு செலீஇயர்); Karikal Valavan appears there only as the victor at Venni. 'The same king at both ends of grief' is built from a colophon name and a passing mention.

222 never says what 'come' (வா) meant or that anyone was dying. It says only that the poet was left behind until the son was born (புதல்வன் பிறந்தபின் வா ... என்இவண் ஒழித்த அன்பிலாள). Reading it as a bar from dying with the king depends on tradition and 223, not on the poem. Ak 55's companions who died with Cheralathan then 'explain' a feeling the poem does not state, so the link is stretched from the colophon.

The two treat Death differently: in Naladiyar 20 it is அருளில்கூற்று that takes even the unborn, while 226 has Death begging like a bard (பாடுநர் போலக் கைதொழுது ஏத்தி, இரந்தன்று ஆகல் வேண்டும்). But 226 is a praise conceit that still concedes the king was taken (வளவற் கொண்ட கூற்றே). It does not deny anyone's powerlessness before Death, so the incompatibility teaches claims is overstated.

This is the same situation, the man hurrying home for evening: Ak 234 வல்விரைந்து ஊர்மதி ... புல்லென் மாலை, Kural 1268 மாலை அயர்கம் விருந்து. Teaches only restates the situation ('the evening return was the fixed goal'). The poem's specific turn, timing his speed by her loosening the braid (பின்னுப்பிணி விடவே), is not something the Kural sharpens or answers.

Both are the stock thurai வினைமுற்றிய தலைமகன் தேர்ப்பாகற்குச் சொல்லியது. The contrast teaches draws is partly true: 34 has the stag that feeds and guards his doe (மடப்பிணை அருத்தி ... துஞ்சுபுறம் காக்கும்), and 344 has எல்லிடை உறாஅ அளவை. But 'the promised hour' is the marker's inference, since 344 states no promise. And 34 has its own clock in the parrot taught to say இன்றுவரல் உரைமோ. Neither poem develops the other.

Pari is named in both. 113 ends with the bard leaving Parambu to seek husbands (பாரி மாய்ந்தென ... மகளிர் ... கிழவரைப் படர்ந்தே), and 200 makes the offer (பாரி மகளிர் ... நினக்கியான் கொடுப்பக் கொண்மதி), both under Kapilar's name. The textual continuity is real, and teaches' errand carried through as a sequence of poems is specific and true.

The image is distinctive and shared: a girl's cry while gathering vengai brings men with bows (48 வேங்கை கொய்குவம் சென்றுழி / 'புலிபுலி!' என்னும் பூசல்; 52 பொன்னேர் புதுமலர் வேண்டிய குறமகள் ... பூசல் ... சிலையுடை இடத்தர் போதரும்). But neither poem calls the cry a custom. And 'that 52's heroine now wants kept secret' joins two different poems' heroines into one story: 52's secret is her love-sickness (பசலை காம நோய்), not a meeting.

Both arrive at not asking. Kural 1061 values இரவாமை even from those who give gladly (கரவாது உவந்தீயும்), and 376 reaches it through one patron's sufficiency (அற்றை ஞான்றினோடு இன்றின் ஊங்கும், இரப்பச் சிந்தியேன் ... தோன்றல் செல்லாது, என் சிறுகிணைக் குரலே). Teaches names the difference exactly: self-respect versus a gift that ends the need, from the giver's side.

Both are Mamoolanar paalai poems, and both draw on Cheralathan's sea and kadambu victory. 347 uses the drum made from it (கடம்பு அறுத்து இயற்றிய பண்ணமை முரசின் கண் அதிர்ந்தன்ன கவ்வை) for the gossip's noise, and 127 uses the tribute hoard (பணிதிறை தந்த பாடுசால் நன்கலம் ... நிதியத்து அன்ன) for the wealth he will not stay for (வழிநாள் தங்கலர்). Teaches is accurate and specific.

The rite is distinctively shared: Ak 35 பதுக்கை ... நடுகல் பீலி சூட்டித் துடிப்படுத்து, and Pur 264 பதுக்கை சேர்த்தி ... அணிமயிற் பீலி சூட்டிப் ... கல், both for men who fell over cattle. Teaches is true: 264 measures the loss through the bards still on the road (இன்றும் வருங்கொல், பாணரது கடும்பே), and in 35 the same stones mark the flesh-smelling road (புலவுநாறு அருஞ்சுரம்) the daughter took.

Both name the Alankanam victory: 23 ஆலங் கானத்து அமர்கடந்து அட்ட, and Ak 175 கைவண் செழியன் / ஆலங் கானத்து அமர்கடந்து உயர்த்த / வேலினும் பல்ஊழ் மின்னி. The note says what the akam poet does with it: the spear measures the lightning of the rains he promised to return by. 'Stock image within the poets' own generation' generalises from one use, but the central teaching holds.

Both personify Death by its timing: 41 காலனும் காலம் பார்க்கும், and Naladiyar 36 இன்றுகொல் அன்றுகொல் என்றுகொல் ... பின்றையே நின்றது கூற்றம். Teaches is specific and true: Death's waiting is the measure the king exceeds in a war boast, and its unknown hour is the spur to virtue in the moral book. But neither limits the other; it is one figure used in two domains.

Both pair rain with something else that sustains the world: 107 மாரியும் உண்டு, ஈண்டு உலகுபுரப் பதுவே, and Naladiyar 97 பெயற்பால் மழைபெய்யாக் கண்ணும் உலகம் செயற்பால செய்யா விடினும். But Naladiyar 97 says only that 'the world does what it should'; reading that as human giving comes from the commentators. And making the later Naladiyar the 'background' for 107, with 107 'centuries before', is a chronology neither text gives.

The two match precisely: 71 அன்பின் அவையத்துத், திறன்இல் ஒருவனை நாட்டி, முறை திரிந்து மெலிகோல் செய்தேன் ஆகுக, and Kural 507 காதன்மை கந்தா அறிவறியார்த் தேறுதல் / பேதைமை எல்லாந் தரும். Fondness as the cause of placing the unfit is in both. Teaches is true and specific: in 71 the act ranks among a king's self-curses beside parting from his wife, losing his friends and losing his birthright.

Both close on மடங்கல் உண்மை மாயமோ அன்றே. 363 ends முந்நீர் வரைப்பகம் முழுதுடன் துறந்தே, and 366 counsels work by day, drink with women and giving (அங்கள் தேறல் ... விடை வீழ்த்துச் சூடு கிழிப்ப). The note correctly makes the tension depend on துறந்தே meaning renunciation of rule, and teaches, that the refrain was shared stock and the counsel each poet's own, is specific.
links.text_issue: purananuru:366 lines 7, 12, 16 and 21 are broken, and editions differ on 16 and 21.

links.reason: Tribute decides the man's fate in both: 44 பகைவரும் தம்திறை கொடுத்துத் தமர்ஆ யினரே frees him to drive home, while in 84 the king அருந்திறை கொடுப்பவும் கொள்ளான், சினம்சிறந்து and he stays in the camp as the rains come. Teaches names a specific puram hinge on which the mullai return turns, which neither poem shows alone.

Azhumbil is named in both: Ak 44 uses சென்னி அழும்பில் அன்ன அறாஅ யாணர் as a measure of plenty, and 283 has அழும்பிலன் அடங்கான் தகையும். But 283 is too broken to say who resists whom, or whether அடங்கான் is the Azhumbil man at all. Building 'defiance in war poetry' against 'prosperity in love poetry' on that fragment overreaches.
links.text_issue: purananuru:283 lines 7 and 12 have gaps, and line 3 differs between editions.

links.reason: Thithiyan is named in both, with different faces. In 322 his hill is the measure of the unattainable girl (கடுந்தேர்த் திதியன் ... புகலரும் பொதியில் போலப் பெறலருங் குரையள்). In 331 his sword against the Velir is the measure of the waste (வேளிரொடு பொரீஇய கழித்த வாள்வாய் அன்ன வறுஞ்சுரம்). Teaches is specific: each speaker takes the face of the king that fits her or his trouble. 'Abandoned wife' slightly overstates 331's speaker.

poems.note: The parrot refusing milk, the idle playmates and the unoffered doll are literal signs of the house's grief for the foster mother; they imply nothing about the lovers.
The flood that defeats even a musth elephant is the literal danger of the night path, a force and not an act a person of the situation does.

iraicchi.act: the bees rest with their mates in the flowering grove (துணையொடு வதிந்த), and the hero ties his chariot bells so as not to disturb them
iraicchi.sense: a man who spares paired creatures their rest is himself hurrying back to rest with his own mate, so the friend's assurance that he is coming is borne out

poems.note: The tender act belongs partly to the hero (மணிநா ஆர்த்த), but the paired bees carry the sense.
A Purananuru poem (perunthinai), so both fields are null by rule, though its weeping woman is an akam figure.

iraicchi.act: the small hare wakes from sweet sleep, goes with its mate (துணையொடு போகி) and drinks at the little pool in the yard
iraicchi.sense: the hero, his work done, longs for the same easy companionship with the woman whose longing exceeds his own

iraicchi.act: the male vulture picks the eyes from the dead and pours them out for its mate (வல்வாய்ப் பேடைக்குச் சொரியும்)
iraicchi.sense: even the vulture provides for its mate where she is, which implies the man should stay and care for his own and not leave her for wealth

poems.note: The vulture is first a figure of the road's horror; its sense rising for the lovers is a reading that the rule permits but does not force.

iraicchi.act: the crab drags off a fallen jamun fruit and lays it in its root-hole for its mate (வீழ்துணைக்கு இடூஉம்), which the hero points out as good (நற்பாற்று இது)
iraicchi.sense: the hero wishes to provide for her and live with her as the crab does with its mate, that is, he means marriage

poems.note: The hero names the crab's act as good but does not state the moral, so this counts as iraicchi rather than an open comparison.
The iruppai flowers falling like dice on the rock are looks only; Kamur is an open simile (போல).
The bear clan raiding iruppai flowers is the road's scene, and no one-sentence sense for the lovers follows from it without strain.

The old stag scattering flowers so that the slope looks like the velan's veri ground could map his visits onto the exposure and divination to come, but neither the poem nor the thurai states that situation.

ullurai.anchor: மதியேர் ஒள்நுதல் வயங்கிழை ஒருத்தி ... நும்மொடு ஊடினள்

poems.note: The heron sleeping while young mango shoots stroke it maps to the man lulled by a new woman's caresses (heron to man, young shoots to the young woman). The tortoise basking on the bent cane belongs to the same mapped scene.

iraicchi.act: the stag calls his doe to the rice fallen from the bamboo (கலைபிணை விளிக்கும்)
iraicchi.sense: a male that will not take his find without his mate implies that the lover will not go without her, as he has now said (இவளொடு செலற்கு)

poems.note: A second carrier, the போகில் feeding its mate a cotton pod (lines 8-9), also meets the rule; the stag was chosen as the first and clearer.
The donkeys are unloaded by the salt merchants, which is something done to them; they do nothing a lover does.

iraicchi.act: the war elephant strains and breaks its tethering post
iraicchi.sense: the man in the camp strains as the elephant does to be loosed and go home to the woman, if only the king would release them

poems.note: The breaking of the post may be only a stock epithet of a war elephant; the rule's four conditions are met, but the reading is thin.

iraicchi.act: the bull elephant caresses the young cow who has just calved, and they sleep on the plantain slope
iraicchi.sense: the pair settled together with their young implies the wedded life the heroine wants from the hill lord, who now comes only by night

poems.note: The cowherds coming home with their herds in the rain are people, not a native thing, and the poem draws the contrast openly in lines 11-15 (தம்நிலை அறிந்தனர் கொல்லோ).
The ஆளி tearing an elephant's tusk is the peril of his path; the mother as tank-guard is an open simile (போல).
The monkeys leaping on bamboo scatter seed that pops on the hot rock: this is scene and sound, with no act of the lovers.

Tusker to hero, tiger killed at the water to the danger or enmity he overcomes, and the cow-elephant joined in sleep to the heroine: the scene answers the praise that he is fit for her. The pair's union is part of that mapped scene.
The fallen ilavam flowers looking like lamps or morning stars are looks only.

ullurai.anchor: குறுந்தொடி மடந்தையொடு வதுவை அயர்ந்தனை என்ப அலரே

poems.note: The varaal tearing the aambal and kuvalai, tangling the vallai and refusing the angler maps the man, the women he spoils and the wife who cannot restrain him. The bull simile (கதச்சேப் போல) joins the fish to a beast, not to a person.
The herons' cries are sound that marks the cold season, not an act.

iraicchi.act: the stag drinks clear water and rests secure with his lovely mate (காமர் துணையொடு ஏமுற வதிய)
iraicchi.sense: the hero, his work done, hurries to rest in the same security with the woman who has kept faith with him

poems.note: The elephant's limp trunk resting on its brow like a snake on a rock is the look of the exhausted road.
The bears spreading over the road strewn with iruppai and konrai pods are the scene of the daughter's path; no sense for the lovers follows in one sentence.
The vulture hurrying to feed its young, whose dropped meat feeds the jackal, could point either to a provider's duty or to the uncertainty of getting, so no single sense can be stated.
The elephant eating the athiral from the cairn's kongu is scene, and the doll (பாவையின்) is an open simile.
